_comment: Copy this file to data/artifacts/{folder}/{id}.json. `type` is the literal artifact storage type (registry | file). `category` is an ARRAY of one or more section titles this artifact belongs to, written as the LITERAL poster section title (e.g. "External Device/USB Usage", "Application Execution") — not a slug. Most artifacts have exactly one, but a few genuinely belong under two sections (matching the SANS FOR500 poster's own cross-listing, e.g. Jump Lists appears under both "Application Execution" and "File and Folder Opening") and should list both. Valid values are the 15 titles used across the corpus — check data/artifacts-manifest.json for the current canonical list before inventing a new one. The physical folder an artifact file lives in is just a kebab-case slug of its first category and is not itself meaningful data. Locked schema, 16 fields exactly — see feedback_artifektx_schema memory.
name: Human-readable artifact name
os_min: Earliest OS version this artifact applies to, e.g. Windows 8
purpose: One to two sentences: what this artifact records and why it exists
normal_baseline: What this looks like on a clean, unremarkable system
anti_forensic_notes: How this artifact is commonly cleared, evaded, or is inherently unreliable — and what that absence itself signals
interpretation: Analyst decoding guidance that doesn't fit the fields above: sub-key/value meanings, format quirks, capacity limits, what this artifact proves vs doesn't prove. Leave as empty string if there's nothing beyond what purpose/key_fields/anomalies already cover.
